summary.en: Jordan has resumed airstrikes in southern Syria against Daesh militants, prompting Syrian authorities to condemn the raids as a breach of airspace and to report civilian casualties. Syrian security forces killed a French jihadist in a shootout in Harem and another French fighter in Idlib, while unidentified gunmen killed two Syrian defence ministry personnel in Idlib. The two sides have reopened the Nasib border crossing and agreed to a joint security committee and investigation into the strikes. The conflict produced 2,732 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Jordan har gjenopptatt luftangrep i sørlige Syria mot Daesh-militante, noe som har fått syriske myndigheter til å fordømme raidene som et brudd på luftrommet og rapportere sivile tap. Syriske sikkerhetsstyrker drepte en fransk jihadist i en skuddveksling i Harem og en annen fransk fighter i Idlib, mens uidentifiserte skytevåpen drepte to ansatte i det syriske forsvarsdepartementet i Idlib. De to sidene har åpnet Nasib-grenseovergangen igjen og blitt enige om en felles sikkerhetskomité og etterforskning av angrepene. Konflikten førte til 2 732 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Aftermath of the Syrian civil war
background.extract: Disputes and clashes in Syria have continued following the fall of the Assad regime in December 2024, which many sources consider the end of the Syrian civil war. Numerous actors are involved, including clashes between the newly-formed Syrian caretaker government and later the Syrian transitional government led by the former emir of Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham (HTS) and incumbent president Ahmed al-Sharaa, Assad loyalists, Alawite groups, and Druze insurgents; clashes between elements of the Turkish-backed Syrian National Army (SNA) and the government on one side, and formerly the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) on the other; as well as an Israeli invasion and occupation of the demilitarized buffer zone in southwestern Syria.
